Hmm, wait — resp1 is only 47KB? A complete plan with bounds/ages/pred for 512×512 should be about 5-10MB… This plan is probably hitting a `guard_ns: None` path (matrix is null). Also, a 4096×512 replay with zero sends completes fine in under 15 seconds for both requests combined ✓.

Just to be safe, let me also test max-size plan and audit with a safe guard (a large output matrix). Use a fabric where a safe guard exists: zero drift, anchors everywhere → peak is about 0 → smallest guard is safe → matrix is complete. big_fabric has random drift up to 1e6 — peak is huge → guard is null. Let me quickly build a variant: N=512, P=512, drift 0, anchors cover all phases of node0, links exist; guard [0, ...]. Then check plan + audit timing (worst-case runtime with 8-9 Dijkstras + complete pred).

Actually scale.py was using random drift. Easiest thing: monkey-patch — build the fabric with big_fabric, then zero out drift_ppb/heat and anchor all nodes with [i,0,P].

content.text: Max-size with a *safe* guard (full matrices + 9 Dijkstras + audit), the true worst case:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
import json, sys, random, time
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/tmp'); sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/submission')
import scale, algo
rng = random.Random(5)
prof, x = scale.big_profile(rng, K=64, M=512)
fabric, P = scale.big_fabric(rng, N=512, P=512, Q=8, per_slice=1024, nguards=8)
fabric['drift_ppb'] = [0]*512
fabric['heat'] = []
fabric['anchors'] = [[i,0,P] for i in range(512)]
fabric['reconfig_ns'] = 0
fabric['guards_ns'] = sorted(random.Random(3).sample(range(0, (fabric['slice_ns']-1)//2), 8))
t0=time.time(); plan = algo.compile_plan(prof, fabric); t1=time.time()-t0
print('plan %.1fs guard=%s warmup=%s bytes=%d' % (t1, plan['guard_ns'], plan['warmup_cycle'], len(json.dumps(plan))))
t0=time.time(); r = algo.audit(prof, fabric, plan); t2=time.time()-t0
print('audit %.1fs' % t2, r)
assert r == {"valid": True}
PYEOF
